segments.title: Chương 292: 0294
segments.content:
Bian Guanyue didn't go to Chen Guiliang's home right away. Instead, she took him to her grandparents' old house.

That area belonged to Huaxing Zheng Street, right in the city center. Large "Demolish" characters were written everywhere, and some buildings had already been torn down.

"The next time I come back, this place will probably be all construction sites," Bian Guanyue said with a tone of infinite melancholy.

The streets and alleys were still the familiar ones, but their appearance was completely changed.

Most of the old neighbors had moved away, with only a few holdout households still sticking it out. The entire street was cold and deserted. All the shops were closed, and some had notices with new addresses posted.

Bian Guanyue pointed to a tube-shaped apartment building and said, "That's where I lived since I was a child. Now they say it's a condemned building and no one's allowed in. Let's take a picture together here."

Bian Guanyue had come prepared, even bringing a digital camera.

She wanted to get a photo with her boyfriend before the building was demolished, as if to make it seem they had lived here together.

Chen Guiliang walked to the open space in front of the building, put his arm around Bian Guanyue's slender waist, and smiled at the camera.

"Click, click!"

Yang Shuo held the camera and continuously pressed the shutter button.

Demolition on this street had already partially begun last year, and it was certain to be completely torn down this year.

But the economic benefits had nothing to do with Bian Guanyue. Before her grandparents passed away, they left their savings to Bian Guanyue, while the old house was left to her aunt.

On the way back, Chen Guiliang saw that she was in low spirits and comforted her, "This is the city center. Old, rundown neighborhoods like this are bound to be demolished sooner or later. If your grandparents' spirits are watching over you, they would definitely want you to live in a better house."

"I'm just a little sad," Bian Guanyue said. "They started talking about demolition here back in '05. When I came back last summer vacation, it was basically all settled. Now that I'm back for winter break, all the neighbors have moved out. The snack stalls I used to visit on my way home from school, I have no idea where they've all gone."

Chen Guiliang held her hand and patted the back of it, a silent form of comfort.

Bian Guanyue leaned into Chen Guiliang's embrace. "I haven't had many things since I was little, so I cherish every single one. Losing one means one less. The house is going to disappear along with my grandparents."

There was an undertone to her words. Chen Guiliang held her and said, "I can't make up for what you've lost, but I will make sure you have more in the future."

"Mmm." Bian Guanyue closed her eyes, feeling that she could rely on Chen Guiliang's chest.

The two of them, along with Yang Shuo, went to the villa belonging to Bian Guanyue's parents.

Her stepmother was as warm and kind as ever. Her stepmother's brother and his wife were also there, as were Bian Guanyue's aunt, uncle, and female cousin.

Since Chen Guiliang was coming, everyone simply decided to celebrate an early New Year together.

Her cousin, Qiao Na, was the first to report to Chen Guiliang, the investor, "After taking over the factory, we were running at a net loss for the first four months. But starting from the fifth month, we've broken even. Everything is on the right track now, but we're mainly making money through contract manufacturing for others. Our own children's clothing brand is developing rather slowly, and we're still working on expanding the market and developing clients."

"Being able to make a small profit from contract manufacturing is already good. You can develop your own brand slowly," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue's uncle, Qiao Weidong, expressed his dissatisfaction with his daughter, "You have a big business right here at home, yet you insist on starting your own company. You're just looking for hardship where there is none."

Qiao Na rolled her eyes at her father.

Bian Guanyue's stepmother's brother had been forcibly stripped of his executive position by Bian Jinsong. He threw a tantrum for a while but was now forced to reconcile, running a small budget hotel to get by.

When this man was a company executive, although he funneled all sorts of money into his own pockets, he was smooth and very perceptive.

He chimed in with a grin, trying to smooth things over, "Hey, Third Brother Qiao, it's a good thing for young people to want to go out and make their own way. With that rascal of mine, I'd be content if he'd just skip a few fewer classes. Qiao Na is so good, starting her own business right after graduating from college. And she's doing quite well at it."

Qiao Weidong said scornfully, "What the hell does she know! She'll only learn her lesson when she runs the factory into the ground."

Qiao Na retorted, "Chen Guiliang is even younger than me. Look how big his company has become."

"Can you compare yourself to him? You study hard every day and only got into a second-tier university. He's at Peking University!" Qiao Weidong still looked down on his daughter. He preferred his illegitimate children.

Chen Guiliang smiled and said, "My admission to Peking University was a special enrollment for my writing. It was a bit of a fluke, nothing special."

Bian Guanyue's stepmother was surprisingly familiar with Chen Guiliang. "Your Gaokao score was above the line for Tsinghua and Peking University. Besides, Gaokao scores don't mean much. To do business, you have to look at personal ability. You're much more capable than us uncles and aunties. You even made it onto the Hurun Rich List last year. Your uncle has been in business for half his life, and he can't get on that Hurun list to save his life."

Bian Jinsong didn't speak, just smiled and smoked.

His group's total assets, after several years of rapid development, were already approaching one billion. But they were mainly fixed assets like hotels, land, and real estate, and he also owed the bank a mountain of debt.

The shares Bian Jinsong held were worth about five hundred million, and he had always been one to make a fortune quietly.

Bian Guanyue's stepmother's brother asked curiously again, "I heard internet companies all make money by going public. When will your company, Xiao Chen, go public?"

Chen Guiliang said, half-jokingly, "We have plans for it, but it's hard to say when exactly it will happen."

Bian Guanyue's uncle, Qiao Weidong, asked, "The conditions for listing in the US should be different from listing in China, right?"

Chen Guiliang explained in detail, "China's requirements for listing are stricter. Even for the SME Board, you need to have sufficient profits. The US has a few different standards. Those with sufficient profits can list based on their earnings, like KongZhong. You can also do it based on shareholder equity and IPO market value. If my company were to list in the US, it would use the non-profit standard. Besides, even in the US, the NYSE and Nasdaq are different. The NYSE has a higher threshold, so Chinese internet companies generally list on the Nasdaq."

Everyone was very interested in listing on the Nasdaq and quickly asked for specific details of the standards.

Watching her boyfriend surrounded by relatives and becoming the center of attention, Bian Guanyue sat happily to the side.

Qiao Na said in a low voice, "These people are such sycophants. If your boyfriend's business wasn't so successful, they wouldn't be this enthusiastic. I've seen right through them a long time ago."

"Mmm." Bian Guanyue nodded in agreement.

Qiao Na added, "Your dad is an exception. He's always doted on you. Half the reason you lived with your grandparents as a child was that you were too stubborn."

Bian Guanyue didn't respond.

She didn't like this new home and avoided coming if she could. Even when she returned to Rongcheng during university breaks, she spent most of her time renting a place outside.

Bian Jinsong suddenly spoke up, "That game company of yours seems to have a new game that's very popular recently."

"You even know about this, Uncle?"

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Actually, it's still a semi-finished product. We just released it early for stress testing. We've only opened registration for a thousand people for now. After the next game update, we'll expand it to three thousand."

Bian Jinsong was clearly keeping a close eye on his daughter's boyfriend. "If it's a semi-finished product, how come I see so many media outlets and websites praising your new game?"

Chen Guiliang explained, "You can tell a tree's nature from the sapling. Even though it's just a semi-finished product, you can still see some signs of what's to come. The quality of the game is very high. That's why the gaming media and players are so excited about it."

"How much monthly revenue does that game company of yours bring in?" Qiao Weidong asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "It's not a large scale. Currently, it's over twenty million."

Qiao Weidong said, "That's already very good. The game is already developed, and there aren't many regular costs, so you can just lie back and rake in the money."

Chen Guiliang just smiled, not bothering to explain.

Without your own sales channels, if you rely entirely on collaborating with other platforms, the channel fees and top-up transaction fees would take up thirty to forty percent of the total revenue.

How could one just lie back and rake in the money?

Part of Youxi Kexue's current monthly revenue of over 20 million came from the Youfutong payment platform.

But for people in traditional businesses, once a game was launched and became a hit, it was as good as lying back and raking in the money. They didn't even know that servers and bandwidth required a huge amount of expenditure.

Bian Guanyue's aunt said, "I've played Xiao Chen's new game. It's quite interesting, 'Plants vs. Zombies'."

"Mom, you play games too?" Qiao Na asked in surprise.

Her aunt said, "Guanyue recommended it. I've played 'Happy Farm' too."

Bian Guanyue's stepmother said in surprise, "'Plants vs. Zombies' was made by Xiao Chen? Qiangqiang (Bian Guanyue's younger brother) is also playing it. He said a classmate introduced him to it. I thought it was interesting, so I've been playing with him recently."

The spread of "Plants vs. Zombies" was truly fast, and the emergence of pirated versions further accelerated the game's circulation.

Over 95% of players were playing the pirated version!

From New Year's Day to the eve of the Spring Festival, it had already found its way onto tens of millions of computers. If this continued, it would inevitably become a national-level game, the kind that even old folks would play a few rounds of in their spare time.

Even many internet cafes had proactively downloaded and installed pirated versions of "Plants vs. Zombies."

The women went to the kitchen with the nanny to get busy, and before long, a table full of "grand dishes" was served.

The atmosphere was quite harmonious, or at least it appeared to be.

The female elders were busy putting food on Chen Guiliang's plate, treating him like the family's future son-in-law.

After the meal, Chen Guiliang sat for a while longer before getting up to leave, borrowing a car from Bian Guanyue's family on the way out.

Bian Guanyue left with him, saying she was going to her maternal grandparents' house for the New Year.

Yang Shuo was in the front seat, responsible for driving.

Chen Guiliang had been made to drink some alcohol and was leaning back in the rear seat with his eyes closed to rest. Bian Guanyue was nestled in his arms, resting.

About halfway through the journey, the expressway ended, and the rest of the way consisted of bumpy national and provincial roads.

As they swayed into the territory of Longdu, Yang Shuo asked, "Should we drop off Miss Bian in the county town first?"

Bian Guanyue didn't answer.

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's all go back to the village together."

Bian Guanyue still didn't say anything, but she was secretly laughing while lying in Chen Guiliang's arms.

Chen Guiliang said, "My grandma likes Sichuan opera too. You two can chat about it."

"Okay, I'll sing for Grandma," Bian Guanyue's smile grew wider and happier. "Which opera does she like?"

Chen Guiliang said, "As long as it's you singing, she'll definitely like all of them."

"Then I'll sing my best piece." Bian Guanyue was as sweet as if she had eaten honey, feeling that all her past efforts in learning to sing opera had not been in vain.
